## Natural history notes

A medium-sized burrowing mammal characterized by its armored body, pointed snout, short legs, strong claws, and long tapering tail. In Florida, it is commonly found in forests, pine flatwoods, hammocks, pastures, lawns, roadsides, and other disturbed areas with loose soils for digging. It is mostly active at night and feeds mainly on insects, grubs, worms, and other small invertebrates, often leaving shallow foraging holes as it searches through soil and leaf litter.
